newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 14.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Health-welfare minister Lee Sung-ho sacked for bribery scandal involving his wife. Representative Sohn Hak-kyu of the ruling New Korea Party named to replace Lee.

- Former health-welfare minister Lee Sung-ho's wife arrested for accepting 170 million won in bribe from lobbyist representing an association of opticians. Ex-minister Lee was questioned by prosecutors, but allowed to go home.
- A North Korea boat with 84 aboard, mostly women and children was rescued by a Chinese fishing boat after being spotted adrift in Chinese waters.

- An association of opticians handed 30 million won each to a government party lawmaker and a former finance and economy minister in exchange for lobbying to win exclusive rights to market eye-glass frames but the money was returned. The two are expected to be summoned for questioning.
- Health Minister Lee Sung-ho replaced in wake of bribery scandal involving his wife.
